clue.text: Test bank book

parts.note: to test something is to prove it, as in proving a theory
RBS is the Royal Bank of Scotland

explanation.surface: An exam paper set on banking, or a passbook from the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test bank' reads as one phrase, but it splits into a verb and an abbreviated bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbs is one of the books of the Old Testament in the Bible.

clue.text: Damaged pot contains remains of Afghan people

definitions.note: the answer is their language, or an adjective meaning of them

indicators.note: contains means holds inside, so one piece sits within the other
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then its letters rearranged
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A broken urn holds the ashes of an Afghan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' reads as human remains in the urn, which suits the surface, but it is the burnt residue.
explanation.definitionFit: Pashto is the language of the Pashtuns, one of the main ethnic groups of Afghanistan.

clue.text: 0-0 score with boring exchange of passes

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so these pieces go inside the outer pair

parts.note: the two zeros read as letters
a net score is a final tally after deductions
W is an abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A goalless draw is dull, even with some neat passing.
explanation.walkthrough: O(NET W)O. 0-0 reads as a football score, but the zeros are two letters O.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a one-two is a quick give-and-go between two teammates passing the ball.

clue.text: Lethal big waves in pool

indicators.note: waves move water about, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dangerously large waves in a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' suggests swimming, but it is the cue game.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight-ball is the most common form of the game of pool, named after the black ball.

clue.text: SLUG NEWS? They can reduce friction

parts.note: a slug is a bullet, and ball is an old word for a bullet
N, E, W and S are the four compass bearings

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about slugs, followed by an engineering tip.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make SLUG NEWS look like a headline; each word is to be replaced by what it stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball bearings are small steel spheres that let parts roll rather than rub, cutting resistance in machinery.

clue.text: Clean house again
Was in front after own goal, and gave dirty look

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the following abbreviation

parts.note: OG is the standard football abbreviation for own goal
a team that was in front led

explanation.surface: A footballer went ahead thanks to an own goal and glared at the opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: A dirty look suggests a glare, but here it is a lecherous one.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone with obvious sexual interest, a leering glance.

clue.text: Victor rejects taking clothes off for nobleman

indicators.note: taking clothes off strips the outer layer, so the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to discount an idea is to reject it

explanation.surface: A man named Victor refuses to undress for an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a British peer ranking below an earl and above a baron.

clue.text: Old compilers run to the front to get loopy prizes

indicators.note: run is R, as in cricket scoring, and that letter is lifted out and put at the front

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
crossword compilers are called setters

explanation.surface: Retired crossword setters race ahead to collect crazy awards.
explanation.walkthrough: O plus SETTERS gives OSETTERS; the last R moves to the front. 'Loopy' suggests mad, but describes the ribbon loops.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosettes are circular ribbon badges, made of looped fabric, awarded as prizes at shows.

clue.text: Swede meets girl, one's controlling mentor

parts.note: Sven is a typical Swedish man's name
gal is an informal word for a girl
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A Swedish man starts dating someone who turns out to dominate his life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' suggests the vegetable or nationality, but here it is a stock Swedish first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali, the hypnotist in du Maurier's novel Trilby, has become the name for any manipulative, domineering guide.

clue.text: Conservative doesn't win in quiet residential roads

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
someone who doesn't win loses

explanation.surface: A Tory candidate is defeated in the leafy suburban streets.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a close is a short dead-end street of houses, typically peaceful and residential.

clue.text: Very brief protest against pay, perhaps to do with response to nuclear attack

definitions.text: to do with response to nuclear attack

parts.note: a second is a very brief moment
a strike is a walkout, often in protest about wages

explanation.surface: A short walkout over wages, possibly linked to a nuclear crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks pay as only one reason for a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-strike describes a nation's capacity to retaliate with nuclear weapons after surviving an enemy's first blow.

clue.text: Idiot welcomes Oscar, namely

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a twit is a foolish person
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A fool greets a man called Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: TW(O)IT: the O sits inside TWIT.
explanation.definitionFit: 'To wit' is an old legal phrase that introduces a specification, meaning 'that is to say'.

clue.text: Dictator's propagated way to produce prairie turnip

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone who dictates, speaking words out for another to write down

parts.note: plants or animals that are propagated are bred
a route is a way to somewhere, said the way that rhymes with boot

explanation.surface: A tyrant spreads a method for growing a prairie vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' suggests a tyrant, but it means a person speaking dictation, signalling words heard rather than read.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadroot is the common name of a North American plant with a starchy edible tuber, also called prairie turnip.

clue.text: Exotic vacation axed in scheme to save money

indicators.note: exotic means strange and outlandish, so these letters appear in an unfamiliar arrangement

parts.note: the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A foreign holiday gets cancelled as part of a plan to cut costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scheme to save money' reads like household budgeting, but it defines a legal way of paying less tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Tax avoidance is arranging one's affairs legally to reduce the tax bill, keeping more cash.

clue.text: What wrongdoer owes to Spooner: crockery?

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words trade places

parts.note: a wrongdoer is a sinner, and what is owed is a debt, with its silent b

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what a criminal owes the Reverend Spooner, perhaps some plates.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of sinner and debt (said as 'det') to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner set is a matching collection of plates and dishes for serving meals, a kind of tableware.

clue.text: American spotted problem, in general

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
to spot something is to see it
to be in a hole is to be in trouble

explanation.surface: An American noticed an issue in the broader picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken as a whole means considered overall, in a broad sense, ignoring the details.

clue.text: Very quick writer held up by erotic dancing

indicators.note: in a down clue being held up by something means sitting on top of it

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themselves as me

indicators.note: dancing moves around, so the letters of the next word change places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fast author is delayed by a racy dance routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteoric means like a shooting star: sudden and rapid, as in a meteoric rise.

clue.text: Period of time with Truss mixing gin is enthralling

parts.note: a spell is a period of time, as in a cold spell

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together, so the following word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: to truss is to tie up or bind
taken as written

explanation.surface: Liz Truss's brief time in office spent mixing gin cocktails was gripping to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes Truss the former UK prime minister Liz Truss, but it is the verb meaning to tie up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spellbinding holds attention completely, as if casting a spell on its audience.

clue.text: Cushion eggs in Italian city

parts.note: a pad is a soft cushion
ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: Packing eggs in soft padding while visiting an Italian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Padova is the Italian name of Padua, a university city in the Veneto region.

clue.text: Raunchy and extremely sexy nursing group

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one piece is cradled inside the other
extremely points to the extremes of a word, its two ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
a team is a group working together

explanation.surface: A racy scene involving a very attractive group of nurses.
explanation.walkthrough: S(TEAM)Y: the group sits inside the ends of sexy.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy describes something erotic or sexually charged, such as a steamy love scene.

clue.text: Go with Man Friday after supper?

parts.note: to go, informally, is to urinate, or wee
a man is a piece in chess, such as a knight

explanation.surface: Robinson Crusoe going off with his companion Man Friday.
explanation.walkthrough: Man Friday is Crusoe's servant, but the phrase splits: Man is a chess piece and Friday belongs to the definition. The question mark flags Friday evening as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Friday after supper is an evening falling on a working day of the week.

clue.text: Husband in lovely position

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the following word

parts.note: nice means pleasant or lovely
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband in an enviable situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a suitable role or place, as in finding one's niche in a career.

clue.text: Precise demand

definitions.meaning: first meaning: accurate in every detail
second meaning: to require or extract

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a phrase about a specific request; they are two unrelated senses of one word, adjective and verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means strictly correct and accurate, while the verb means to insist on obtaining something from someone.

clue.text: Iris or Declan or Tim?

parts.note: taken as written
Declan Rice is an England footballer and Tim Rice a lyricist; both share this surname

explanation.surface: A quiz question: which of three people with first names fits?
explanation.walkthrough: Iris looks like a third first name alongside Declan and Tim, but it is the definition, the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Orrice is a variant spelling of orris, a type of iris whose fragrant root is used in perfumery.

clue.text: "Scattered community essentially hard work" stated revolutionary

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the whole string is read in the opposite direction
essentially points to the essence or core of a word, so only its central letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of the word
OP is short for opus, a musical work
to state something is to say it

explanation.surface: A revolutionary declares that building a scattered community is basically hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a slogan, but the words split into a definition and pieces to be turned round: AROPSAID backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is a people dispersed far from their original homeland, such as the Jewish or Irish communities abroad.

clue.text: Artist reaches out after Australian expelled

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered here, so the letters are rearranged
expelled means thrown out, so that abbreviation is removed from the other word

parts.note: taken as written
A is a standard abbreviation for Australian

explanation.surface: A painter makes a gesture of welcome once an Australian has been thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reaches out' reads as a phrasal verb, but out is the signal to rearrange the letters left after A goes.
explanation.definitionFit: M. C. Escher was a Dutch graphic artist famous for impossible staircases and tessellations.

clue.text: Undated Daily Record follows leading collection of fabulous animals

indicators.note: undated means without a date, so the abbreviation D for date is removed
follows means comes after, so this piece is placed after the next one

parts.note: the leading one is the best
a diary is a daily record of events

explanation.surface: A newspaper, the Daily Record, follows the leading paper without a date on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Record is a Scottish newspaper, which makes the capitals look like a title; here it is a plain description of a journal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestiary is a medieval book describing real and mythical beasts, often with moral lessons.
